name: Jozabad
overview: Jozabad was a male Levite noted in Scripture for having married a foreign wife. His identity as a Levite places him within the tribe set apart for service to God, and his marriage to a foreign woman is specifically mentioned in Ezra 10:23. No additional personal details or notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jozabad means 'YHWH bestowed,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's provision. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 10:23 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Jozabad as a descendant of the tribe of Levi. Beyond this tribal affiliation and his marriage to a foreign wife, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Jozabad's mention in Ezra 10:23 highlights the issue of intermarriage between Israelites and foreign women during the post-exilic period, a significant concern for maintaining covenant purity. As a Levite, his actions would have held particular weight given the Levites' role in upholding the spiritual and ceremonial standards of Israel. His inclusion in the list underscores the communal effort to address and rectify breaches of the covenant in returning to faithful worship of God.
